sections.voiceover: On February 4, 2025, a Canadian National freight train derailed near Emo, Ontario on the Fort Frances Subdivision. Why are pre-2003 railcar wheels with rims prone to shattering such a dangerous safety risk?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Emo, Ontario and the Fort Frances Subdivision route.
sections.sfx_cue: Ambient wind and distant train whistle.
b_roll: Aerial view of Canadian National rail tracks in Ontario

sections.voiceover: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada warns that unknown numbers of these aging wheels remain active.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a manufacturing date stamped into a metal rail wheel.
b_roll: Close-up of metal stamping on industrial rail equipment

sections.voiceover: Investigation report R25W0010 confirms these aging components cause catastrophic derailments across the Fort Frances Subdivision. Canadian National operations near Emo, Ontario face ongoing risks from these brittle, outdated railcar wheels.
sections.visual_cue: Document cover of TSB report R25W0010 on a desk.
b_roll: Footage of freight train wheels moving on tracks

sections.voiceover: Rail safety remains compromised because these pre-2003 wheels are still rolling on tracks today.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of a freight train passing through a rural landscape.
b_roll: Freight train passing through rural Ontario landscape
